newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Ports, Shipping and Rehabilitation (East) Minister Mohammed Ashraff says the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels will be able to move swiftly in the eastern Ampara district in the event of a confrontation between the Moslem and the Sinhalese population there.

Sirisena Cooray, a former minister in the previous United national Party (UNP) government who was arrested last week under the country's emergency laws, has not been questioned in connection with an alleged plot to kill President Chandrika Kumaratunga as reported in the state media, his lawyers say.
President Kumaratunga says crushing the LTTE militarily is a precursor to peace in Sri Lanka.
President Kumaratunga says the government has little choice but to neutralise the LTTE militarily before embarking on a political solution to the 13-year-old ethnic crisis.

The details of an alleged plot to harm President Kumaratunga will be disclosed in the next few days. The evidence regarding the plot, uncovered during police investigations into the activities of Sirisena Cooray, are now being out together, sources in the Criminal Investigation Department say.
Sri Lanka arrests a soldier in the army's intelligence wing who was allegedly passing key information to LTTE rebels for the past five years.
University staff to get a salary hike next month. The government says it has allocated 60 million rupees for the increases.
Police still questioning former heavyweight minister Sirisena Cooray, who is alleged to be involved in a plot to assassinate President Kumaratunga.
Police likely to take into custody more people said to be involved in a plot to kill President Kumaratunga.

Health Minister Nimal Sripala de Silva says government to hire 155 doctors to serve in hospitals in northern Jaffna, eastern Trincomalee and Batticaloa and western Mannar districts. Hospitals there have been facing a shortage of doctors for a while.
